parsed.explanation: No trans-specific presentation or facility law is documented, and the last state raid is from 2010, so this is not in the organised-targeting tier. However the combined regime criminalises conduct a trans visitor may be read as engaging in under Articles 520/517 up to three years, irrespective of marker, with no anti-discrimination recourse, unregistrable organisations, documented fear and whispers, hostile political endorsements, and dated armed-group beatings, torture and claimed executions. That hostile, no-recourse context makes the sexuality statute a live secondary lever, while present enforcement, trans-specific policing, facilities, custody and care are largely undocumented.

entry_documents.exposure: Articles 520 and 517 reach men and women alike irrespective of legal marker; same-sex conduct carries up to three years.
entry_documents.protection: No anti-discrimination protection documented; no complaint route after a document dispute.
entry_documents.interaction: A passport or presentation dispute could be reframed under the criminal provisions, with no relief route documented.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: June 2010 raids arrested over 25 men, mostly charged with homosexual acts; no later state raid is documented.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Private-gathering enforcement shows the statute has been used, but its current frequency and any trans-specific custody practice are not established.

care_services.exposure: Official stigma is documented, including a 2005 deputy minister calling HIV/AIDS divine punishment for homosexuality.
care_services.protection: State runs voluntary HIV testing clinics and limited school education; no comprehensive LGBTQ education.
care_services.interaction: HIV prevalence figures are not sourced to trans-specific care access and are not treated as a care-denial rate.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Political actors endorsed tougher laws and one armed-opposition figure said he would not object to stoning homosexuals; another leader rejected gay rights claims.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Hostile framing increases the practical risk of the criminal provisions being applied to a person read as same-sex or gender-nonconforming.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Beatmegs and torture by named armed groups are documented; at least 16 killings were claimed by a jihadist group as of June 2016 and at least 30 executions reported by another group.
street_violence_police_response.protection: No police protection or prosecution of attackers is documented in the dossier.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Armed-group violence occurred mainly in areas under their control and the raw counts lack denominators or comparison with general homicide, so their current traveller rate is unresolved.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Legal gender recognition is unavailable, LGBTI organisations cannot register, and no anti-discrimination law exists; criminalisation removes the complaint route.
remedies_unknowns.protection: April 2025 advocacy reporting debunked a specific claim that LGBTQIA+ people were being hunted in one city.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: The debunk weakens evidence of a current hunting campaign but does not establish present state enforcement, facilities, custody or care practice.

anchor_checks.comparison: Higher than 0.25-A because that anchor has current, repeated police raids, detention and extortion against trans people; here state enforcement is dated to 2010 and no trans-specific police campaign is documented.

Similar to 0.45-C in lacking a universal facility rule but having widespread no-recourse exposure; lower or comparable because criminal penalties up to three years and hostile armed violence add severity beyond service discrimination.

Materially lower than 0.65-C because that anchor has documented traditional acceptance and a dead-letter same-sex offence with no lever use; here there is no documented acceptance, a used statute, hostile endorsements and no recourse.

parsed.synthesis: The operative risk is not a documented trans-specific universal ban but a criminalised, hostile and remedy-free environment in which a trans visitor could be read under same-sex and indecency provisions. Current trans-specific policing, border practice, facilities, custody and care are undocumented, and the most recent enforcement and armed violence are dated, so the dossier does not support the severe or high targeting tiers. Nevertheless, the three-year exposure, historical party raids, social fear, hostile official framing and absence of any complaint route keep the combined regime well below reduced-risk jurisdictions with acceptance and working protection.
